One-sentence judgment: brickmasons and blockmasons do not "carry bricks"; they lay brick, block, and structural tile with mortar according to drawings and setting-out lines, control vertical and horizontal by course, build corners, point the joints, and ensure the dimensions and quality of the wall and structure. On the U.S. side this corresponds to O*NET-SOC 47-2021.00, listed as Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0). The core boundary is this: you can complete setting out, laying, cutting, and pointing work, but you cannot replace design, supervision, or structural safety judgment, nor move to the next process without a briefing against the plan and acceptance.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to check the drawings, dimensions, and process requirements, record and report material or survey point problems honestly, and accept correction; the real outdoor, standing, carrying, and height loads must be observed separately in safe formal training. A single paper result cannot judge long-term physical adaptation or physical quality.

Start with the MA-01 fictional paper exercise on this page and use the complete problem statement and answer to check drawing reading, quantity calculation, recording, and question reporting. No site, equipment, or mentor is needed; if you are still interested, then check the safety conditions and mentoring of formal practical training. The paper exercise does not prove physical masonry, independent construction, or acceptance ability.

Education, qualifications, and position authorization must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2, and among respondents 70% think a high school diploma or equivalent is required, 13% think less than high school, and 13% think some college without a degree; BLS lists the typical entry path as an apprenticeship or on-the-job learning. These are survey and public-source bases; in mainland China, construction involves the Construction Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Safety Production, among others, the project leader of a construction unit should be a person who has obtained the corresponding practice qualification, and workers must receive safety production education and training.

This is a skilled trade centered on reading drawings and setting out, laying and building corners, material use, cutting and pointing, self-inspection, and collaboration; proficiency does not confer the right to design changes or process acceptance. U.S. wages and employment are for the precise occupation SOC47-2021; for China only the NBS2025 construction industry unit average proxy is shown, and the releases checked in this round do not list occupational wages and employment separately.

The work of this occupation can be divided into three categories: first, preparation and setting out (interpreting drawings and specifications, measuring and marking the setting-out lines from datum points, calculating angles and courses, and checking material specifications and quantities); second, laying and installation (spreading mortar, laying brick and block, building corners and controlling with lines, cutting and trimming, fixing with clamps, anchors, or pouring as the structure requires, and building arches and openings); third, finishing and checking (removing excess mortar, pointing and tooling the joints, checking plumb and surface flatness, and cleaning and handing over the work face). All three share the same traceable quality chain.
Preparation and setting out

Interpret the drawings and specifications to determine the specifications → measure and mark the setting-out lines from datum points → calculate angles and courses → check the material and mortar requirements → set up the course pole and stretch the control line → confirm the working conditions and safety measures with the foreman.
Laying and installation

Spread the mortar → lay brick and block and correct vertical and horizontal course by course → build the corners first and then stretch the line to fill the middle → cut, trim, and open holes as needed → fix and anchor as the structure requires → control the joint thickness and fullness → complete arches and special parts.

Remove excess mortar and work the joints with a pointing tool to obtain a uniform, sealed appearance, check plumb, surface flatness, and joint quality, clean the work area and hand the completed part over to the next process, and report deviations or material problems honestly.

Brickmasons and blockmasons mainly build brick and block structures; stonemasons 47-2022 process and install stone, carpenters 47-2031 handle wood structures and installation, floor layers 47-2042 lay floor covering materials, and tile and stone setters 47-2044 handle hard finishes. Architectural and engineering managers 11-9041 organize architectural, engineering, or research and development activities, and cannot be written as an ordinary foreman or construction manager. Similar trade names do not mean responsibilities or training are interchangeable.
Core purpose
Lay brick, block, and tile into walls and structures that are dimensionally accurate, plumb and flat, with full and uniform mortar joints, according to drawings and specifications.
Main objects and basis

The objects are materials such as brick, block, structural tile, glass block, and mortar, and parts such as masonry structures, partitions, arches, and pipe shafts; the basis is the construction drawings and design description, the masonry and construction acceptance specifications, the mortar and material requirements, and the on-site safe work and protection rules.
Core process

Reading drawings and setting out, material checking, mortar mixing and use, laying and corner building, cutting and trimming, anchoring and fixing, pointing and cleaning, and self-inspection of plumb and surface flatness.
Main outputs
Plumb, flat masonry and finish parts whose dimensions and joints meet requirements, plus traceable work and self-inspection records and material use and leftover stock count records.
Responsible party

Articles 19, 26, and 36—38 of China's construction quality regulations set out the quality responsibilities of the design unit, the construction unit, and the supervisor respectively, and the construction unit establishes a quality responsibility system and process inspection; the supervising engineer's signature and the chief supervising engineer's signature are different statutory steps. Crews and workers carry out the work, self-inspection, and reporting according to their actual positions; Article 21 of the safety regulations makes the project leader responsible for the project's safe construction, and personal self-inspection does not replace unit inspection or the supervisor's signature.
Authority and approval

Whether you can enter the work face, whether you can adjust the mortar mix or the laying method on your own, and whether you can move to the next process are determined by the construction organization design, the safety technical briefing, and the process acceptance flow, and do not arise by themselves from proficiency or years of service.
Boundary of conclusions

A self-inspection conclusion states that "this section of work completed the day's process according to the drawings and specifications"; it does not equal acceptance of the subdivisional work, nor does it replace structural safety and design judgment, and it is affected by material batch, mortar condition, and temperature.

Before starting the job, check at least six items: the position basis and form of employment, the training and apprenticeship path, the materials and processes actually used, personal protection and work-at-height arrangements, the process acceptance and wage settlement method, and the real method of pay and work hours.
Occupational basis

Mainland China already has the mason occupational code 6-29-01-01, and the official catalog lists the 2023 national vocational skill standard; this page does not infer from the name that it corresponds one-to-one with U.S. O*NET-SOC 47-2021.00. Specific positions are checked against the masonry object, the process, the employing unit, and the working conditions; an occupational classification code does not equal a construction safety qualification.
Education and training path

O*NET Job Zone1—2, SVP below 6.0; in the education requirement question, 70% answered high school or equivalent, 13% below high school, and 13% some college without a degree, which are position requirement answers, not the educational composition of workers or a universal entry threshold. The typical BLS entry is a high school equivalent and apprenticeship training, and the OOH describes an apprenticeship or on-the-job learning; the below-high-school answer comes from O*NET and is not attributed here as a direct OOH conclusion. Specific program admission requirements must be checked separately.
Methods and tools

The details page lists 7 software categories, and the Hot single page lists 4 products: Office and Excel each appear in 1% of unique U.S. job postings in 2025, and the QuickBooks and Windows ratios are not published and are not filled in as 0. Estimating, CAD, and structural calculation products are in the details list, not additional products listed on the Hot page; the 7 categories and the 4 products are not the same indicator, and neither is an adoption rate, a required skill, or an AI substitution rate.
Safety and work permits

The work involves outdoor and weather exposure, work at height and scaffolding, cutting dust, heavy lifting, and noise; check the provision and inspection requirements for personal protective equipment (hard hat, safety shoes, goggles, gloves, and hearing protection, and where necessary a fall-arrest harness and respiratory protection), and the approval and monitoring arrangements for work at height and near edges.
Training and regulatory requirements

In mainland China, construction work is regulated by the Construction Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Safety Production: the construction unit must establish and improve a safety production responsibility system and a safety production education and training system, the project leader should be a person who has obtained the corresponding practice qualification, and workers must receive safety production education and training and use protective equipment as required.
Pay and work hours

The same position title may be paid by the day, by piece (per square meter or per brick), or monthly, and is affected by stoppages and overtime caused by the schedule and the weather; when comparing, put the method of pay, quantity confirmation and settlement cycle, idle-time and waiting pay, travel and accommodation arrangements, and personal protection costs into the written agreement.

Brickmasons and blockmasons (U.S. side O*NET-SOC 47-2021.00) use mortar and other materials to lay and bond building materials such as brick, structural tile, concrete block, cinder block, glass block, and terra cotta block to construct or repair walls, partitions, arches, sewers, and other structures; they use trowels, levels, plumb bobs, and measuring tools, control vertical and horizontal by course, and calculate the materials needed from drawings. The tasks include material handling and carrying, but are not only carrying; the occupational definition does not automatically grant the right to design or structural safety conclusions. O*NET also lists kiln and refractory masonry, demolition of damaged brick, and a new drone inspection task, so the object cannot be limited to ordinary house walls.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET-SOC 47-2021.00 Brickmasons and Blockmasons, page updated 2026, Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), and this occupation is not marked Bright Outlook. The official duties are to "lay and bind building materials, such as brick, structural tile, concrete block, cinder block, glass block, and terra cotta block, with mortar and other substances to construct or repair walls, partitions, arches, sewers, and other structures"; there are 15 tasks in total (12 Core, 2 Supplemental, 1 New; the importance of the new drone inspection item is not published), and the highly important tasks include measuring and marking the setting-out lines from datum points (93), building corners and controlling courses with lines (89), spreading and smoothing mortar (87), calculating angles and courses and determining vertical and horizontal (84), cutting brick and block (83), and interpreting drawings and calculating materials (82).

paragraphs: This page compares brickmasons and blockmasons with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and output, key differences, and which direction suits each preference. The adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupational descriptions and do not mean the trade names are interchangeable.

Evidence note: the career directions and core outputs are based on the official descriptions of O*NET 47-2021.00 and related occupation lists and are on the U.S. basis; the qualification, licensing, and safety requirements of adjacent trades must be verified separately by their own jurisdiction, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut to a career change.

The table below compares brickmasons and blockmasons with adjacent trades and the paths for moving in from adjacent positions; the basis for judgment is the main output, what the role is responsible for, and the training required, rather than how similar the trade names are.
Stonemasons (47-2022.00)
Process and lay natural and manufactured stone, with stone finishes, countertops, and masonry as the main output.

The two crafts are related, but stonemasons center on selecting, processing, and installing natural stone and require higher material grain and processing precision; brickmasons and blockmasons focus on volume laying of brick, block, and tile and on dimensional control.
If you prefer stone processing and fine installation, look first at stonemasons; if you would rather do volume masonry and exterior walls, look first at brickmasons and blockmasons.
Carpenters (47-2031.00)
Build wood structures, formwork, doors and windows, and interior finishes, with wood components and installation as the main output.

Carpenters center on timber and wood-based composite materials and formwork systems, and the work methods and tools differ; brickmasons and blockmasons work with mortar and block and are more sensitive to plumb, joints, and mortar condition.
If you would rather do wood structures and finishes, compare carpenters first; if you would rather do masonry and exterior walls, look first at brickmasons and blockmasons.
Floor Layers (47-2042.00)
Lay block, strip, or sheet floor covering materials for shock absorption, sound insulation, or decoration.

Floor layers 47-2042 focus on floor coverings; brickmasons and blockmasons 47-2021 focus on brick and block structures. The materials, substrate, and installation methods differ, and a transfer requires checking the target training.
If you would rather do floor and finish laying, compare floor layers first; if you would rather do wall and structural masonry, look first at brickmasons and blockmasons.
Tile and Stone Setters (47-2044.00)
Lay tile and stone finishes, with wall and floor finish layers as the main output.

Setters center on thin-bed bonding and finish precision and usually do not take on masonry structures; brickmasons and blockmasons take on masonry structures and appearance quality and must anchor and fix according to structural requirements.
If you care more about finish appearance and precise joint alignment, look first at setters; if you would rather do load-bearing and enclosing masonry, look first at brickmasons and blockmasons.
Architectural and Engineering Managers (11-9041.00)
Plan, direct, or coordinate architectural, engineering, and related research and development activities.

Architectural and engineering managers 11-9041 manage technical activities and teams; brickmasons and blockmasons mainly lay masonry on site. The manager path requires a target technical field and management ability, and crew leadership experience cannot be treated directly as an engineering management qualification.

If you prefer organizing and deciding on architectural or engineering technical activities, you can study that management direction's education, experience, and duties further; if you prefer the physical masonry craft, you can look at this occupation first.
Moving in from labor employment or an adjacent trade
You already have site assistance, carrying, or plastering experience and want to move to standardized masonry work.

The gap is usually not physical strength but drawing reading and setting out, course and plumb control, judging mortar condition, cutting and pointing technique, and process self-inspection and safety rules; having been around a site does not mean you can lay masonry independently.

If you are willing to start as an apprentice and accept a master's mentoring and quality checks, you can consider moving in; if you only want to work by the piece without learning setting out and quality requirements, the gap will be large.

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the main output, what the role is responsible for, and the training required, not how similar the names are; once the direction is set, check the training and qualification requirements of the target trade, the materials and processes actually used, the safety protection arrangements for work at height and outdoors, and the form of employment and settlement method item by item, and keep written confirmation.

paragraphs: Boundary: this section describes occupational risk and responsibility boundaries, not an evaluation of an individual or institution; the specific statutory obligations and handling procedures are determined by the applicable jurisdiction, the construction organization design, and the employment relationship.

The main risks include falls, scaffolding or lifting injuries, dust and noise, carrying loads, and process quality problems. Working conditions, collective protection, engineering controls, safety briefings, and suitable personal protection must be put in place; a mask or experience alone is not enough. The specific project controls are determined by the responsible personnel under the applicable requirements.

Evidence scope: the risk and boundary entries are based on the official tasks, work activities, and work context of O*NET 47-2021.00, the O*NET training and education information, the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration construction industry materials, and public materials on the Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Safety Production; they do not cover a specific project's internal rules.
Workers and crews
Falls from height, being struck by equipment, or heavy lifting injuries may have serious consequences.

Check briefings, provision of protection, and equipment management under Articles 27 and 32—35 of China's safety regulations; workers check the usable condition and report, and their own observation cannot serve as scaffolding erection acceptance or a professional inspection qualification. On-site collective protection and the specific attachment conditions are checked against the actual plan.
Erecting or using scaffolding without following the briefing, no edge protection, and a safety belt not attached.

Masonry dimensional deviation, under-filled joints, or improper anchoring will cause rework and quality hazards.

Verify dimensions and joints according to the drawings and technical standards; out-of-limit reporting, rework, or suspension is handled according to the actual process duties. Articles 28—33 of the quality regulations cover unit inspection, the prohibition on using nonconforming materials, and training, and the editorial checking steps do not grant resumption or acceptance authority.
Skipping setting out and self-inspection to meet the schedule, or continuing to lay when nonconforming materials are found.
Workers and everyone on site
Long-term dust, noise, and outdoor exposure may cause cumulative health damage.

First check the dust exposure and engineering controls for the material and the work, such as wet methods or effective dust extraction measures meeting equipment requirements; respiratory protection, hearing protection, training, and health surveillance are provided under the applicable rules. The OSHA construction silica dust requirement is in the U.S. jurisdiction and is not directly a Chinese compliance conclusion.
Lacking effective dust control or exposure checking, continuing to cut and chip with only an ordinary mask; respiratory protection also cannot replace engineering and work controls.
Construction unit and project leader

In mainland China, the construction unit must establish and improve a safety production responsibility system and a safety production education and training system, and the project leader should be a person who has obtained the corresponding practice qualification; failure to do so may lead to administrative penalties and accountability.

Under the Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Safety Production, implement safety education and training, safety technical briefings, and inspection records, and have a qualified project leader organize safe construction.

When the division of employment and safety responsibility is unclear, tracing accidents and quality problems is easily blocked.

Article 24 of the safety regulations: the general contractor bears overall responsibility for site safety, the general contractor and the subcontractor bear joint liability for the safety of the subcontracted work, and the subcontractor is subject to the general contractor's management; clarifying rights and obligations in the contract cannot exempt statutory responsibility. items.title: What evidence employers usually look at

values: MA-01: paper exercise pack

All editorially fictional, with tools limited to pen and paper or a spreadsheet. The drawing V2 is a front-view rectangle 2400×1000 mm with the lower left corner as the origin; the grid is 200×100 mm per cell, 12 columns wide and 10 rows high, with columns numbered from left to right and rows from bottom to top. The opening occupies columns 5—7 and rows 4—7, with the range x=800—1400 and y=300—700 mm, 600 wide and 400 high. Each grid cell counts as 1 fictional quantity module, the dimensions already include the module boundaries, no joint allowance is added, and it does not represent real brick size.

Quantity rule: deduct the complete grid cells of the opening; add a 5% reserve to the net module count and round up. Only the front-view area and paper modules are counted, not wall thickness, staggered joints, real mortar, opening lintels, or procurement waste.

The fictional judgment limits of self-inspection table V2: plumb deviation ≤3 mm and level deviation ≤4 mm, and any item over the limit means that point needs correction; the values are used only for record comparison in this exercise and are not project acceptance limits. Initial check A=(2,3), B=(4,2), C=(3,5); re-check A=(2,3), B=(2,2), C=(3,4), with the brackets ordered plumb/level. Document check record: D1 drawing V2 confirmed, D2 material description V1 not confirmed, D3 working conditions column blank.
Your delivery

Draw the 12×10 grid and mark the opening, and list the total area, opening area, net area, net module count, module count with reserve, and the units; calculate from the problem statement and do not look up real construction data.

List separately whether the initial check and re-check A/B/C meet the stated conditions, and mark the out-of-limit dimensions; write the D1/D2/D3 status and the next verification request. Keep the initial check values and do not overwrite them with the re-check, and do not claim the documents are complete just because the re-check meets the conditions.
Reference review

Total area 2.4 square meters; opening 0.24 square meters (3 columns × 4 rows = 12 cells); net area 2.16 square meters, net modules 120−12=108; 108×1.05=113.4, rounded up to 114, with a reserve of 6. The opening is at columns 5—7 and rows 4—7, with boundaries 800/1400 and 300/700 mm.

Initial check A meets both items; B plumb 4>3 needs correction, and C level 5>4 needs correction. The re-check A/B/C all meet the stated conditions, and C still meets them with both items equal to the limit. D1 is confirmed; D2 requires checking the material description version corresponding to drawing V2 and obtaining confirmation; D3 requires adding actual working condition information. A passing re-check does not resolve the pending items D2/D3, nor can it be used to conclude that the physical wall passes.
Exercise use and boundaries

MA-01 only observes drawing understanding, unit conversion, quantity calculation, records, and question reporting habits; no real site, masonry tools, or master is needed. This problem does not design load-bearing, detailing, mortar, cutting, scaffolding, or physical construction plans, cannot be used to apply fictional judgment limits to engineering, and grants no operating qualification, process acceptance authority, or independent masonry ability. Real training requires separate safety conditions and mentoring.
Position requirement checklist

List the target jurisdiction, work content, safety education, corresponding operating qualification, mentoring, authorization, and pay settlement separately; when there is no target unit information, write pending verification and do not invent answers.
Keep training, skill performance, safety conditions, operating certificate, and acceptance authority separate; MA-01 cannot replace any of those practical qualifications.
Independent review record
Complete MA-01 first without looking at the answer, then check the 108 net modules, the 114 modules with reserve, and the A/B/C records, keeping the first version and the reasons for corrections.

It can be completed without external review; you may optionally ask a teacher to look at the paper records, but feedback not actually received cannot be written as having obtained a master's acceptance.
One-page learning review
Note the MA-01 editorial fiction, the V2 drawing, your calculations, the difference between the initial check and the re-check, the D2/D3 pending questions, and the correction process.

Write only the paper tasks completed and the observations; physical training not done should be stated clearly, and agreement with the reference answer must not be packaged as construction experience.
Tool use note
When using a spreadsheet or AI, list the tool, the input, the formula, and the manual review; the rounding of 108×1.05 and the handling of values equal to the judgment limit must be reproducible.
You can also hand in a pen-and-paper process without tools; tool output must not be treated as drawing confirmation, material approval, or actual process acceptance.

rows: Before applying
Check the form of employment, project type, safety assurance, and method of pay, and prepare supervised practical training records.
A record noting the work content and self-inspection data; able to explain clearly the difference between a masonry position and a plastering or floor laying position.
Do not treat having been around a site as proof that you can set out and accept work independently, and do not promise duties beyond your training scope.

Able to first explain the order of stopping work, reporting, and handling according to the briefing; able to state your own uncertainty clearly.
Do not promise experience, qualifications, or performance that cannot be verified in the interview.
Probation period
Complete setting out, laying, and pointing under a master's mentoring, and accept item-by-item checks on courses, plumb, and joints.
Dimensions and courses meet requirements, joints are uniform and full, self-inspection records are complete, and deviation handling is documented.
Do not independently enter work at height or edge work beyond your training scope, and do not adjust the mortar mix or the process without authorization.
90 days after onboarding
Check according to plan whether safety education records, protection provision, and pay settlement are in place, and assess operating discipline and collaboration style.
Check which parts you can complete according to actual training and authorization, and proactively report when information is incomplete; do not presume independent competence from 90 days.
Authorization and the settlement method must be confirmed in writing, not replaced by verbal promises.

values: Understanding the occupation
Read this page's tasks and adjacent occupations; write the duty differences between 47-2021 and stonemasons, floor layers, and engineering managers, noting the source and jurisdiction.
Check safety and qualifications

From this page's sources, list the differences between safety education, briefings, protection, the corresponding special operations certificate, and acceptance authority; raise questions to verify with a future target unit, and do not enter a site to operate.
Drawing and quantity calculation

Following MA-01, draw the 12×10 grid and the opening, and independently calculate the total, opening, and net areas and the net module count and the module count including the reserve; save the calculation process before checking the answer.
Check the initial inspection records
Judge A/B/C under the stated rules of ≤3 / ≤4, and write out the out-of-limit dimensions for B and C; keep the original values and the pending-correction status, and do not build a physical wall.
Check the re-check and the documents

Compare the two measurement records and handle values equal to the limit item by item; list D1 as confirmed, D2 version as pending verification, and D3 conditions as not filled in, and explain that a passing re-check does not resolve the document gaps.
Review and revise

Independently check against the answer and the drawing coordinates, and keep the errors and the reasons for corrections; external teacher feedback is optional, and if there is none, state it as a genuine self-check.
Decide the next step

Organize the grid drawing, quantity calculation, self-check and re-check, and the pending list, and write the reason for continuing to explore or pausing; if you continue to practical training, check the safety conditions and mentoring separately, as seven paper days do not prove occupational competence.

entries: Continue exploring: if you are willing to check drawings carefully, record deviations, and raise questions, you can study formal training further; completing MA-01 does not prove you can construct independently.
Pause: if quantity calculation or recording is difficult, first locate the unit, coordinate, or judgment problem, then decide whether to build basics or change direction.
Change direction: if you prefer stone processing or finishes, compare stonemasons and tile and stone setters; check the materials, processes, and training separately.

Check employment: check safety education, mentoring, the corresponding special operations qualification, work authorization, and protection item by item, and do not match certificates by the name of work at height or edge work.
Organize the evidence: mark the paper drawing, quantity calculation, records, and revision reasons as fictional; if no physical training was done, do not write practical training results.
Cost assessment: check the specific training, tool, accommodation, and out-of-town construction costs with a real project, and do not fill in unverified fees.

Next step: based on specific questions, find formal training with suitable safety conditions, or first improve drawing reading and quantity calculation; do not automatically expand your duties because seven days have ended.
